proposals.searched: Junker, U. (2004) 'QUICKXPLAIN: Preferred Explanations and Relaxations for Over-Constrained Problems', AAAI-04, pp. 167-172, https://aaai.org/Papers/AAAI/2004/AAAI04-027.pdf ; correctness proof: Rodler, P. (2022) 'A formal proof and simple explanation of the QuickXplain algorithm', Artificial Intelligence Review, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9622537 . PROPOSAL: the 'why it fails' card currently comes from Z3's unsat core, which is not guaranteed minimal and is computed over Z3's encoding rather than Lean's semantics. Run QuickXplain over the experiment's mandatory requirements and coupled relations with the compiled Lean checker as the consistency oracle (isConsistent(S) := the Lean verdict on the profile restricted to S is not REJECT), ordering constraints by CryoLean's trust model (user-entered and adjustable parameters first, manufacturer specifications last) so the returned conflict is the preferred minimal one. 'Lean reports a violation' is monotone in the constraint set (conjunctive semantics), which is QuickXplain's precondition. Add a Lean check 'minimal_conflict' (the set yields REJECT and every one-element removal does not) and, following Rodler's proof, port QuickXplain itself to Lean so the explanation procedure is verified, not only its output.

Liffiton, M.H., Sakallah, K.A. (2008) 'Algorithms for Computing Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets of Constraints', Journal of Automated Reasoning 40:1-33, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10817-007-9084-z ; Liffiton, Previti, Malik, Marques-Silva (2016) 'Fast, flexible MUS enumeration' (MARCO), Constraints 21:223-250, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10601-015-9183-0 . PROPOSAL: report repairs as minimal correction sets (the minimal sets of requirements or parameters that must be relaxed) and reasons as MUSes, using the hitting-set duality (every MCS hits every MUS). In demo B the MCSes include {n_flux_lines}, {n_drive_lines}, {design_margin}; each becomes a Z3 optimisation over only that subset and is re-verified by Lean (REQUIREMENTS_MET on the exact document), replacing the single heuristic suggestion. MARCO's partial enumeration returns the first MCSes quickly at catalog scale (26 configurations x ~20 requirements), and the verdict card can state whether enumeration was complete.

Felfernig, A., Schubert, M., Zehentner, C. (2012) 'An efficient diagnosis algorithm for inconsistent constraint sets', AI EDAM 26(1):53-62, https://tugraz.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/n-efficient-diagnosis-algorithm-for-inconsistent-constraint-sets (preprint https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09005); parallel variant Le et al. (2023) 'FASTDIAGP: An Algorithm for Parallelized Direct Diagnosis', AAAI-23. PROPOSAL: catalog search is a knowledge-based configuration task (C_KB = a configuration's documented capabilities and coupled models, C_R = the user's requirements). FastDiag computes a preferred minimal diagnosis (which user requirements to relax) directly, without enumerating conflicts first, in O(2d log2(n/d) + 2d) consistency checks; run it per configuration when ranking alternatives so near-misses read 'compatible if you relax {temperature >= 1.8 K}'. Consistency checks are Lean runs on reduced documents, optionally pre-filtered by Z3.

Gamba, E., Bogaerts, B., Guns, T. (2023) 'Efficiently Explaining CSPs with Unsatisfiable Subset Optimization', Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.1.14260 ; Bleukx, I. et al. (2026) 'Using Certifying Constraint Solvers for Generating Step-wise Explanations', AAAI-26, https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38432 . PROPOSAL: choose explanations by cost, not only minimality: an optimal constrained unsatisfiable subset (OCUS) whose costs encode evidence trust (citing a manufacturer specification is cheap, a user-entered or inferred value expensive) and readability (single-capability checks before coupled relations). Render it step by step ('3 x (58*13 nW + 50*79 nW + 8*20 nW) = 14.592 uW'; '14.592 uW > 12 uW at 20 mK [ev_bf_0006]'; 'therefore REJECT'), each step an exact rational evaluation Lean already performs; as in Bleukx et al., derive the steps from a certifying proof log so each is independently checked, here by Lean.

JCGM 100:2008 'Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement' (GUM), https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf ; Melquiond, G. (2008) 'Proving bounds on real-valued functions with computations', IJCAR 2008, LNAI 5195, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-71070-7_2 . PROPOSAL: add an 'interval' value kind (lo, hi, basis in {guaranteed, typical, expected, measured with coverage factor}) and give Lean a three-valued interval semantics over exact rationals: PASS only if the requirement holds at the pessimistic end of every interval, FAIL only if it fails at the optimistic end, otherwise NEED_MORE_INFORMATION, with soundness theorems (interval PASS implies PASS for every point value; interval FAIL implies FAIL for every point). Cases found here: Krinner's per-line loads with uncertainties (MXC drive line 0.013(6) uW -> [0.007, 0.019] uW, currently central values only), Bluefors 'Guaranteed 575 uW / Expected 650 uW at 120 mK', OptistatDry cold head 0.16 W (50 Hz) / 0.2 W (60 Hz), DynaCool base 1.8 K (60 Hz) / 1.85 K (50 Hz). Interval arithmetic on rationals is exact and its monotonicity lemmas are easy to prove in Lean.

Scholz, F.W. 'Statistical Tolerancing', University of Washington Stat 498B course notes (2008), https://faculty.washington.edu/fscholz/DATAFILES498B2008/TolerancingStat498B.pdf - contrasts arithmetic (worst-case) stacking TOL_S = TOL_1 + ... + TOL_n with root-sum-square stacking. PROPOSAL: wherever a coupled model adds uncertain terms (wiring heat budget sums, cooldown + run time, working distance + spacers, contraction mismatch), the trusted Lean verdict should use worst-case stacking of interval bounds, which is sound with no distributional assumption; RSS stacking assumes independent, centred, normally distributed errors that vendors do not document, so it should appear only as an untrusted advisory margin (like Z3 output). Show both numbers on the verdict card so users see how much of a rejection comes from conservatism.

Benveniste, A. et al. (2018) 'Contracts for System Design', Foundations and Trends in Electronic Design Automation 12(2-3):124-400, https://doi.org/10.1561/1000000053 (summary https://www.nowpublishers.com/article/DownloadSummary/EDA-053). PROPOSAL: model each vendor figure as an assume-guarantee contract rather than a bare number: '>= 575 uW at 120 mK' under {measured at the experimental flange outside the mixing chamber, empty system, standard shields, default PT415}; '< 1e-5 Torr' under {CCR running, TPS-FRG pump}; '1.8 K base' under {60 Hz mains}. CryoLean's model 'validity' list already encodes one kind of assumption; generalise it so every capability carries assumption predicates over the configuration and experiment (mains frequency, installed wiring, cryostat state). Lean uses a guarantee only when its assumptions are discharged, otherwise NEED_MORE_INFORMATION; contract refinement gives a principled rule for combining a base instrument with an option insert (He-3, DR) whose contract replaces the base temperature and cooling guarantees.

OPC Foundation, OPC 30500-1 'OPC UA for Laboratory & Analytical Device Standard (LADS) - Part 1: Basics', https://reference.opcfoundation.org/specs/OPC-30500-1/4 ; Juchli, D. (2022) 'SiLA 2: The Next Generation Lab Automation Standard', in Smart Biolabs of the Future, Advances in Biochemical Engineering/Biotechnology 182, https://doi.org/10.1007/10_2022_204 . PROPOSAL: define a machine-readable cryostat capability profile aligned with these standards: each configuration becomes a LADS Device with FunctionalUnits (sample temperature control, magnet, vacuum, optical access) whose control-function ranges and engineering units carry CryoLean vocabulary keys, install state and evidence id/hash; expose the same as SiLA 2 Feature Definition (FDL) properties (e.g. MaximumField, CoolingPowerAt). Import: vendor- or facility-published LADS/SiLA descriptions enter CryoLean only as untrusted candidates that must pass the validation gate (quote + source document). Export: facilities publish their exact installed configuration (options, wiring, mains frequency) so verdicts bind to real instruments instead of catalog assumptions.

W3C (2013) 'PROV-O: The PROV Ontology', W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013, https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ . PROPOSAL: record every transformation between the printed value and the Lean input as PROV activities (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:Activity): unit conversion, rounding, fit evaluation, choosing guaranteed over expected, reading an archived snapshot instead of the live page. This research found silent derivation issues that such records would expose: pressure bounds rounded down (1e-5 Torr = 1333.22 uPa stored as 1333 uPa; 1e-4 Torr = 13332.24 uPa stored as 13332 uPa), so the catalog claims a slightly better vacuum than documented. With activities recorded, the validator can enforce 'rounding must be conservative in the key's better direction' and the verdict card can show the derivation chain.

NIST Cryogenic Material Properties, '6061-T6 Aluminum (UNS A96061)' https://trc.nist.gov/cryogenics/materials/6061%20Aluminum/6061_T6Aluminum_rev.htm and '304 Stainless (UNS S30400)' https://trc.nist.gov/cryogenics/materials/304Stainless/304Stainless_rev.htm . PROPOSAL: the thermal_stress model (E*|eps_s - eps_h| <= sigma_allowed) lacks elastic moduli. NIST gives Young's modulus as plain polynomials y = a + bT + cT^2 + dT^3 + eT^4 in GPa (6061-T6: a=7.771221E1, b=1.030646E-2, c=-2.924100E-4, d=8.993600E-7, e=-1.070900E-9, equation range 2-295 K, 1 % fit error; 304 SS: two branches, 5-57 K and 57-293 K). Unlike the log-polynomial conductivity fits, these are exactly representable in CryoLean's expression language (add/mul of operating_temperature with decimal literals), so Lean can evaluate E(T) exactly, with validity bounds equal to the fit's equation range and the 1 % fit error carried as an interval. Store coefficients in materials.json as reference_data; an allowable-stress table is still needed before validating the model.

model_data.claim: CRX-VF documented field-versus-temperature envelope: +/-2.5 T at 10 K; +/-2 T from 11 K to 400 K; +/-1 T from 401 K to 420 K.
CRX-VF vacuum with the standard TPS-FRG pump: below 5e-4 Torr at room temperature, below 1e-5 Torr at base temperature and below 1e-5 Torr at maximum temperature.
CRX-4K vacuum with the standard TPS-FRG pump: below 5e-4 Torr at room temperature, below 1e-5 Torr at base temperature and at maximum temperature.
